005package org.wpilib.util;
006
007/** JNI for alert data. */
008public class AlertDataJNI extends WPIUtilJNIWrapper {
009  /**
010   * High priority alert - displayed first with a red "X" symbol. Use this type for problems which
011   * will seriously affect the robot's functionality and thus require immediate attention.
012   */
013  public static final int LEVEL_HIGH = 0;
014
015  /**
016   * Medium priority alert - displayed second with a yellow "!" symbol. Use this type for problems
017   * which could affect the robot's functionality but do not necessarily require immediate
018   * attention.
019   */
020  public static final int LEVEL_MEDIUM = 1;
021
022  /**
023   * Low priority alert - displayed last with a green "i" symbol. Use this type for problems which
024   * are unlikely to affect the robot's functionality, or any other alerts which do not fall under
025   * the other categories.
026   */
027  public static final int LEVEL_LOW = 2;
028
029  /** Information about an alert. */
030  public static class AlertInfo {
031    /**
032     * Constructs an AlertInfo object. Called from JNI.
033     *
034     * @param group Group name for the alert
035     * @param id Unique ID for the alert
036     * @param text Text description of the alert
037     * @param activeStartTime Time when the alert became active, or 0 if not active
038     * @param level Level of the alert
039     */
040    public AlertInfo(String group, String id, String text, long activeStartTime, int level) {
041      this.group = group;
042      this.id = id;
043      this.text = text;
044      this.activeStartTime = activeStartTime;
045      this.level = level;
046    }
047
048    /** Group name for the alert. */
049    public final String group;
050
051    /** Unique ID for the alert. */
052    public final String id;
053
054    /** Text description of the alert. */
055    public final String text;
056
057    /** Time when the alert became active, or 0 if not active. */
058    public final long activeStartTime; // 0 if not active
059
060    /** Level of the alert. */
061    public final int level; // LEVEL_HIGH, LEVEL_MEDIUM, LEVEL_LOW
062  }
063
064  /**
065   * Gets the number of alerts. Note: this is not guaranteed to be consistent with the number of
066   * alerts returned by getAlerts, so the latter's return value should be used to determine how many
067   * alerts were actually filled in.
068   *
069   * @return the number of alerts
070   */
071  public static native int getNumAlerts();
072
073  /**
074   * Gets detailed information about each alert.
075   *
076   * @return Array of information about each alert
077   */
078  public static native AlertInfo[] getAlerts();
079
080  /** Resets all alert simulation data. */
081  public static native void resetData();
082
083  /** Utility class. */
084  private AlertDataJNI() {}
085}
